title: DR1's address picker puts the whole book on one page and narrows it as the trader types; the frontend shows five records at a time behind a Search button and pages through the rest.

finding.frontend: The picker shows five records at a time — `PAGE_SIZE = 5` (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10), sliced server-side — with a govukPagination block beneath the table (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:64-66) and a secondary Search button that re-posts the whole form (:86-91). fe-address-picker-place-of-origin reads "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" over five rows, then "1 2 3 Next". Because the chosen record can be on a page the trader is not looking at, the picker has to restate it in an inset above the table, "Selected address: …" (:93-95) — a control that exists only to work around the paging. The page carries no client JavaScript by design (:7-11).
finding.prototype: DR1 renders every address for the role in one table with no pagination anywhere on the page, and heads it "Select an address" with a live count, "Showing 9 out of 9 results" (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:93-97). The search control is a `type="search"` input with a magnifier button that does not submit (:70-90); typing in it hides non-matching rows and rewrites the count as the trader types. dr1-consignment-address-select shows all nine records at once, so a chosen radio is always visible next to Save and continue.
finding.difference: Show the whole role list on one page: drop PAGE_SIZE and the pagination block, put the count line above the table, and let search narrow the rendered list rather than fetch a new page. The frontend's stated no-JS baseline is the constraint DR1 does not have — DR1's magnifier button is `type="button"` and a no-JS Enter discards the query, so copying it verbatim would lose a working search for a trader without JavaScript. The portable half is one page, no pagination, count above the table, with the existing server-side search kept as the no-JS fallback and a filter layered on top. The "Selected address:" inset can go once the chosen row is always on screen. This assumes an organisation's book stays small enough for one page; if it will not, the finding is about the count line and the search behaviour rather than about removing pagination.
finding.falsifiedBy: Pagination appearing in DR1's consignment-address-select template, or an address book large enough that one page is not viable.
